entries.caption: Windows service target, 25 runs, before either fix. 18/25 (28% failure). Failures at 48-108s against a 19s baseline, every one with a flat thread and descriptor inventory.
entries.name: 01-before-any-fix

entries.caption: Windows service target, 20 runs, loaded, with worker-fault recording but before the store writer retry. 14/20. This is the run that captured the swallowed StoreError [WinError 5] naming the cause.
entries.name: 02-before-store-fix-instrumented

entries.caption: Windows service target, 100 runs, after the store writer retry and the approval-holding fix. 98/100, longest consecutive 39. Both failures were test_pausing_a_task_waiting_for_consent_actually_stops_it at the normal 19s duration.
entries.name: 03-after-both-fixes

entries.caption: Controlled two-transport experiment on Linux: 20 integration slices over AF_UNIX and 20 over forced loopback TCP, one machine and one workload, only the transport differing. 40/40 passed, peak TIME_WAIT 0 for both. This refuted the ephemeral-port-exhaustion hypothesis.
entries.name: 04-transport-experiment
entries.note: No machine-readable artefact exists for this measurement; the run printed to a console. The caption is the record.

entries.caption: Linux service target, 12 runs as user bunny on ext4. 12/12, with every inventory delta (threads, descriptors, sockets, leases, waiters, live services) exactly zero.
entries.name: 05-linux-service-stress
entries.note: No machine-readable artefact exists for this measurement; the run printed to a console. The caption is the record.
